correctness.rationale: With \(r=1/\gamma\) and \(D=r+\rho-a>0\), the exact box-constrained primal subproblem is \(D\)-strongly convex. In a neighborhood of \((0,0)\) its unconstrained minimizer is interior, giving the exact state matrix \(M=D^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}r&-1\\ \rho r&r-a\end{pmatrix}\). Its trace and determinant are \((2r-a)/D\) and \(r/D\). The three second-order Jury-Schur inequalities reduce exactly to \((\rho-a)/D>0\), \(\rho/D>0\), and \((4r+\rho-2a)/D>0\). Boundary non-attraction is supplied by unit-modulus or \(-1\) eigenmodes of the exact local linear map. The eigenvalue discriminant is \((a^2-4\rho r)/D^2\); monotonicity on its real-root and complex-root sides proves the unique optimum \(r_\star=a^2/(4\rho)\) and factor \(a/(2\rho-a)\). The packaged exact-rational checker verifies all critical identities and representative boundary cycles.

value.rationale: The model isolates a natural normal negative-curvature mode while satisfying the standard composite problem assumptions through a simple box indicator. The result separates two notions that are easy to conflate in proximal augmented Lagrangian design: making every primal subproblem strongly convex versus stabilizing the coupled primal-dual iteration. It gives the exact missing balance, \(\rho>a\) and \(4/\gamma+\rho>2a\), and a unique critically damped local tuning \(\gamma_\star=4\rho/a^2\). This supplies a structural parameter-design benchmark for the recent adaptive P-ALM framework rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
